voice of the last clause (inappropriate shift to passive if "the walls were painted by us")

student_error.Painting the hallway murals were harder: Makes the verb agree with "murals," the nearest noun, instead of the gerund subject "Painting."
student_error.Painting the hallway murals was harder t: Switches to passive voice in the last clause, even though "we" did the painting.
student_error.Painting the hallway murals were harder: Does not track what the subject of each clause is, so gets the agreement and the voice wrong.

item.explanation: Correct: The subject is the gerund phrase "Painting the hallway murals," which is singular, so the verb is "was." The sentence is in active voice with "we" as the doer ("we expected," "we sketched"); switching to "the walls were painted by us" is an inappropriate shift in voice. The option with only the first error breaks the first rule, the option with only the second error breaks the second, and the remaining option breaks both.
item.varied_dimension: agreement with a gerund-phrase subject; shift from active to passive voice

item.correct_answer: After pouring the solution into the test tubes, each group should record the results on the chart, since there are three columns left to fill in.
error_sites: subject that the verbal phrase "After pouring the solution" describes (dangling verbal if "the results should be recorded")
verb in "there ___ three columns" (wrong number if "is")

student_error.After pouring the solution into the test: Uses the passive "the results should be recorded," which sounds formal and scientific, so the opening phrase says the results did the pouring.
Uses "is" because "there is" is the more familiar phrase, not checking the plural "columns" after it.
Writes in a formal-sounding lab style without checking who does each action or what the verb agrees with.

item.explanation: Correct: "After pouring the solution" needs the person who poured as the subject; "each group" poured, the results did not. In a "there" sentence the verb agrees with the noun after it, "three columns," so it is "are." The option with only the first error breaks the first rule, the option with only the second error breaks the second, and the remaining option breaks both.
item.varied_dimension: dangling verbal phrase; subject-verb agreement in a there-clause
